relations.subject: server:bucket
relations.evidence: Deletes a bucket in the cluster. When the bucket is deleted, all indexes on the bucket are also deleted.

notable_absence.finding: Same pattern as the rest of this batch: no RBAC role is named for a destructive, cascading operation (bucket deletion cascades to every index on the bucket) - only the generic unauthorized-error boilerplate under --username/--password. Notably this is the single most destructive command in the batch (irreversible bucket + index removal) and it gets the least access-control framing of any page here - just one sentence of DESCRIPTION total.

cross_component_finding: This is the thinnest page in the batch: the entire DESCRIPTION is one sentence, and every other section (OPTIONS beyond --bucket, HOST FORMATS, CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION, ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES) is the same boilerplate already flagged in couchbase-cli-bucket-compact.json. No new copy-paste duplication beyond what that finding already covers, but the extreme terseness of the one substantive sentence ('Deletes a bucket in the cluster. When the bucket is deleted, all indexes on the bucket are also deleted.') is itself a data point for the authorship-provenance hypothesis: no caveat, no confirmation-prompt mention, no warning register at all for an irreversible destructive action.
cross_product_finding: None found - this page does not reference REST, UI or another product's bucket-deletion vocabulary.
